      "date": "2026-08-21T23:13:23Z",
      "plaintextBody": "Hi Tyson, Thank you for reaching Teal Communications Support Team and for bringing this to our attention. We will investigate the issue from our side to determine why the TLS handshake is timing out despite the TCP connection being successful, we’ll work on and check: Roaming and public-egress issues The SIM’s public NAT/egress IP Outbound and return traffic to 51.143.124.200:443 Any MTU/MSS, fragmentation, firewall, or DPI issues Possible network-side issues with the destination Thank you for your patience and for providing the detailed diagnostics. We’ll investigate further and get back to you with our findings. Regards,  Jacky Teal Support Team

                            On

                            Fri, 21 Aug at 4:09 PM

                            , Tyson Goulding <tyson.goulding@optconnect.com> wrote:

 Hi Teal Support, We're troubleshooting a payment-transaction failure for a customer's terminal in Canada. The evidence points to the TLS handshake failing on the public-egress path for one of our SIMs on the lattigopriv APN, and we'd like your help characterizing what happens on your side. Domains: aprivawebservices.trafficmanager.net & paymentwebservice.apriva.com via 51.143.124.200 The SIM: ICCID 8901990000005060358 (IMSI 204080930355844), assigned IP 100.81.201.96 on the lattigopriv APN. What we see (device diagnostic loop, 2026-08-20, per-phase timing DNS -> TCP -> TLS): - The device resolves and TCP-connects to the payment host (https://www.google.com/url?q=http://ws.accounts.apriva.com&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E -> https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E) in ~0.4s, every cycle. - The TLS handshake then goes silent and times out at 10s, every cycle. TCP up, TLS dead. This is not a device or application problem. The customer put a completely different SIM, from another provider, into the same physical terminal, and the identical payment transaction to the same host completed normally. Same hardware, same app — so the terminal is fine; the failure follows this SIM's connection. The private path is healthy. The device's traffic over our tunnel to the customer datacenter returns HTTP 200 throughout — including during the exact windows the public TLS handshake is timing out. Only the public egress for this SIM is affected. From the device telemetry, we can see our SIM is attaching to a tower that appears to be TELUS-owned, which raises the question of whether a roaming or inter-operator issue is affecting the egress path. Our questions: 1. For SIM 8901990000005060358 / IP 100.81.201.96 on lattigopriv, are there any known roaming or egress issues affecting its public-Internet path — particularly to https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E? 2. What public egress IP is this SIM NAT'd to on the way out, and do you see the outbound TLS session to https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E leaving your gateway with return traffic from the server? 3. Is there any MTU / MSS / fragmentation handling or a stateful firewall / DPI policy on the lattigopriv egress that could drop the larger packets of a TLS handshake while allowing the small TCP handshake packets through? We can share the raw device logs if that would help. OptConncet Network Engineering Team

--

 Tyson Goulding

 Director of Network Architecture
